input.passage: Most glaciers creep forward at a steady pace of a few meters per year. A surge glacier behaves differently. For years or even decades, it moves slowly while ice builds up in its upper reaches. Then, often within a few months, the glacier speeds up dramatically and can advance several kilometers ______ Variegated Glacier in Alaska, for example, surged in 1982 and 1983, moving up to 65 meters in a single day.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 "Then ... the glacier speeds up dramatically and can advance several kilometers downvalley"와 빈칸 뒤의 "The Variegated Glacier ... surged ..."는 각각 독립절이므로 마침표로 분리해야 한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 연결한 쉼표 스플라이스이다. B는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 이어 붙인 융합문(run-on)이다. D는 접속사 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표가 들어가 있어 어색하고 비표준적이다.
input.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("Then ... the glacier speeds up dramatically and can advance several kilometers downvalley") form an independent clause, and so do the words after it ("The Variegated Glacier ... surged ..."). Two independent clauses need to be separated correctly, and a period does that, so C is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B uses no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D puts an unnecessary comma after the conjunction "and," which isn't standard punctuation.
input.design: 빈칸 앞뒤가 모두 명확한 독립절이라 '두 독립절은 쉼표만으로 이을 수 없다'는 규칙 하나로 풀 수 있게 했다. 오답은 쉼표 스플라이스, 융합문, 쉼표를 잘못 쓴 접속사로, 학생들이 흔히 하는 실수들이다.

content.text:
Easy Boundaries item: two independent clauses with comma splice options.

Passage: "In 1894, French army captain Alfred Dreyfus was convicted of passing military secrets to Germany. The evidence against him was weak ______ many officials ignored its flaws because of widespread antisemitism within the army."

Options: A "weak; many" — but must not repeat word before blank. So blank after "weak": options "; many", ", many", "many", ", and, many"? Better: A "; many officials", B ", many officials", C " many officials", D ", which many officials"? D would make "which many officials ignored its flaws" ungrammatical—plausible enough. Keep simple: A semicolon, B comma, C no punctuation, D colon after "many"? Use ", so" no—that's correct too. D: "and, many officials" incorrect comma placement. Fine.

input.passage: In 1894, French army captain Alfred Dreyfus was convicted of passing military secrets to Germany. The evidence against him was weak ______ ignored its flaws, in part because of widespread antisemitism within the army. He was not fully cleared until 1906.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The evidence against him was weak"와 빈칸 뒤 "many officials ignored its flaws..."는 각각 완전한 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 접속사 and 뒤에 쉼표를 두어 구두점 위치가 잘못되었다(쉼표는 and 앞에 와야 한다).
input.explanation_en: The words before the blank, "The evidence against him was weak," form a complete independent clause, and so do the words after it, "many officials ignored its flaws...". You can join two independent clauses with a semicolon, so A is correct. B links them with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, so it creates a run-on sentence. D puts the comma after "and" instead of before it, and that placement is wrong.
input.design: 이 문항은 세미콜론으로 독립절 두 개를 잇는 규칙 하나만 알면 풀 수 있다. 오답은 흔한 오개념을 담았다: 쉼표 스플라이스, run-on, 접속사 뒤에 잘못 놓인 쉼표.

input.passage: In his 1959 book The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life, sociologist Erving Goffman compared social interaction to a theatrical performance. According to Goffman, a restaurant server who smiles warmly at diners is acting on a "front stage," where an audience is watching. Once the server walks into the kitchen, however, the polished performance often ______ to the relaxed, unguarded behavior of the "back stage."
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸의 동사는 단수 주어 "the polished performance"와 수가 일치해야 하므로 단수 동사 D "gives way"가 정답이다. 지문의 다른 문장도 "smiles", "walks"처럼 현재 시제를 쓰고 있어 D와 시제도 맞는다. A "give way"는 복수 주어에 쓰는 형태이다. B "are giving way"와 C "have given way"도 복수형 조동사(are, have)를 써서 단수 주어와 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The verb in the blank needs to agree with the singular subject "the polished performance," so the singular verb in D, "gives way," is correct. D also fits the present tense used elsewhere in the passage ("smiles," "walks"). A, "give way," is the form you'd use with a plural subject. B, "are giving way," and C, "have given way," also use plural helping verbs (are, have), so they don't agree with a singular subject.
input.design: 쉬운 문항으로 만들기 위해 주어와 동사 사이에 수식어 없이 단수 주어 바로 뒤에 빈칸을 두었고, 주어-동사 수 일치 규칙 하나만 적용하면 풀리게 했다. 오답 세 개는 모두 복수형 동사이다.

input.passage: Linguists once assumed that languages spoken by larger populations tend to have larger phonemic inventories—that is, more distinct consonant and vowel sounds. One proposed explanation was that sounds are lost more easily in small, isolated communities. To test this idea, linguist Mira Okonjo compared inventory sizes across hundreds of languages, but she counted sounds in two ways: once by listing every phoneme, and once by grouping phonemes according to shared distinctive features, such as voicing or nasality. When she counted individual phonemes, larger populations did show slightly larger inventories. When she counted feature categories, however, the difference vanished: small and large speech communities used about the same number of features, with large ones simply combining those features in more ways. These findings suggest that ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: small speech communities lose distinctive features more readily than large ones do, which accounts for their smaller phoneme counts.
whether population size appears to influence phonemic inventories depends partly on how linguists choose to count the sounds of a language.
large speech communities tend to develop entirely new kinds of distinctive features that small communities do not use.
phonemic inventory size bears no relationship to population size, no matter which counting method linguists use.
input.explanation: 개별 음소로 세면 인구 규모와 음소 수 사이에 약한 관계가 보였지만, 자질 범주로 세면 그 차이가 사라졌다. 따라서 관계가 드러나는지 여부가 계산 방식에 달려 있다는 B가 가장 논리적이다. A는 소규모 공동체가 자질을 잃는다고 하지만, 지문은 자질 수가 비슷하다고 말한다. C는 대규모 공동체가 새로운 자질을 만든다고 하지만, 실제로는 같은 자질을 더 다양하게 조합할 뿐이다. D는 음소 단위로 셌을 때 약간의 차이가 나타났다는 사실과 모순된다.
input.explanation_en: When Okonjo counted individual phonemes, she found a small link between population size and inventory size, but that link disappeared when she counted feature categories. So whether the link shows up depends on the counting method, which is what B says. A claims small communities lose features, but the text says both groups use about the same number of features. C says large communities invent new kinds of features, but they actually just combine the same features in more ways. D goes too far, because the phoneme count did show a slight difference.
input.design: This is a two-step inference: you have to compare the results of the two counting methods and then conclude that the result depends on the method. The wrong answers each reuse part of the text (the loss hypothesis, the combinations, the vanished difference), and you can only rule them out by reading closely.

input.passage: In Noh, the masked drama that took shape in fourteenth-century Japan, a principal actor may spend several minutes crossing the stage in a sliding walk so slow that the movement is barely visible. Some Western critics have treated this restraint as a sign that Noh is indifferent to emotion. Yet the masks themselves complicate that view: carvers shape each mask so that its expression shifts with the angle of light, and a slight tilt of the head downward makes a mask appear sorrowful, while a slight tilt upward makes it seem to brighten. Because so little else moves onstage, audiences notice even these small changes in angle. This suggests that the minimal movement of Noh ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: lets tiny gestures carry emotional meaning rather than showing that emotion is absent from the form.
lets the masks stay fixed in expression rather than showing that emotion is absent from the form.
lets Western critics judge emotion accurately rather than showing that emotion is absent from the form.
lets fourteenth-century carvers replace actors rather than showing that emotion is absent from the form.
input.explanation: 지문은 가면이 머리 각도에 따라 표정이 달라 보이고, 다른 움직임이 거의 없어서 관객이 그 작은 변화를 알아챈다고 설명한다. 이 두 정보를 연결하면, 최소한의 움직임이 오히려 작은 동작에 감정적 의미를 실어 준다는 결론이 나오므로 A가 정답이다. B는 가면이 '고정된 표정'이라고 하는데, 이는 각도에 따라 표정이 바뀐다는 지문 내용과 반대된다. C는 지문이 비평가들의 견해를 반박하고 있으므로 비평가들이 정확하게 판단한다는 말과 맞지 않는다. D는 조각가를 언급하긴 하지만, 그들이 배우를 대신한다는 근거는 지문에 없다.
input.explanation_en: The passage tells you that a mask's expression changes with the angle of the head, and that audiences notice these small changes because almost nothing else moves onstage. If you connect those two facts, you can see that the restraint makes small gestures carry emotional meaning, so A is correct. B says the masks keep a fixed expression, but the passage says their expression shifts with the angle of light. C doesn't fit because the passage is arguing against the critics' view, so it can't say they judge emotion accurately. D mentions the carvers, but nothing in the passage suggests they replace actors.
input.design: 정답을 고르려면 가면 각도에 따른 표정 변화와 움직임이 적을수록 관객이 더 주목한다는 두 정보를 연결해야 한다. 오답은 모두 정답과 같은 문장 틀을 쓰고 지문의 소재(가면, 비평가, 조각가)를 일부 가져와 그럴듯하게 만들었다.

input.passage: Many shipping lines charge a single flat fee to move a standard container between two ports, no matter how heavy the cargo inside is. A box packed with light pillows costs the same to ship as one filled with dense machine parts. The carrier accepts this mismatch on purpose ______ across thousands of containers, the heavy and light loads tend to average out, so the flat fee still covers the line's typical cost per box.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The carrier accepts this mismatch on purpose"와 뒤 "across thousands of containers, ... per box"는 각각 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 아무 부호 없이 이어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 접속사 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 and와 이어지는 구 사이를 잘못 끊는다.
input.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("The carrier accepts this mismatch on purpose") form an independent clause, and so do the words after it ("across thousands of containers, ... per box"). A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so C is correct. A joins them with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B puts no punctuation between them at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D adds an unnecessary comma after "and," which wrongly cuts the conjunction off from the clause it introduces.
input.design: 독립절 두 개 사이 경계 하나만 판단하면 되는 문제로 만들었다. 오답에는 쉼표 스플라이스, 무종지문, 접속사 뒤 잘못된 쉼표라는 흔한 오류를 넣었다.

content.text:
Easy subject-verb agreement item on the contact hypothesis.

Passage: "First proposed by psychologist Gordon Allport in 1954, the contact hypothesis holds that prejudice between groups can shrink under the right conditions. Studies of desegregated schools suggest that cooperation between students of equal status ______ especially effective at reducing bias."
Subject: cooperation (singular). Answer: is. Options: A) are, B) have been, C) is, D) were. Tense check: "were" is past and plural, and "is" fits the present "suggest". Good.

input.passage: First proposed by psychologist Gordon Allport in 1954, the contact hypothesis holds that prejudice between groups can shrink under the right conditions. Studies of desegregated schools suggest that cooperation between students of equal status ______ especially effective at reducing bias.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 동사의 주어는 단수 명사 "cooperation"이며, "between students of equal status"는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 현재형 동사가 필요하므로 C가 정답이다. A와 B는 복수형 동사로, 바로 앞의 복수 명사 "students"를 주어로 착각하게 만드는 오답이다. D 역시 복수형(were)이고 현재 시제 문맥(suggest)과도 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of the blank is the singular noun "cooperation." The phrase "between students of equal status" just modifies it. That means you need a singular present-tense verb, so C is correct. A and B are plural verb forms, and they're tempting because the plural noun "students" comes right before the blank, but "students" isn't the subject. D is also a plural form (were), and it doesn't fit the present-tense context set by "suggest."
input.design: This is a single-rule subject-verb agreement item with a short prepositional phrase between the singular subject and the verb. The plural noun right before the blank is the trap.

input.passage: When a pond dries up, the tardigrades living in it do not simply die. Instead, these tiny animals curl into a compact shape and lose almost all of the water in their bodies ______ they can then remain in this dormant state, called anhydrobiosis, for years. Researchers have found that special proteins help protect the animals' cells while they are dry.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "these tiny animals ... lose almost all of the water in their bodies"와 빈칸 뒤 "they can then remain ... for years"는 각각 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 접속사 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 문장 흐름을 부적절하게 끊는다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("these tiny animals ... lose almost all of the water in their bodies") and the text after it ("they can then remain ... for years") are both independent clauses. A semicolon can correctly join two independent clauses, so A is correct. B uses only a comma to join the two clauses, which makes a comma splice. C puts the two clauses together with no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D adds an unneeded comma after the conjunction "and," which breaks up the sentence incorrectly.
input.design: 독립절 두 개 사이의 경계를 세미콜론으로 처리하는 단일 규칙 문항으로, 오답은 쉼표 스플라이스, 무종지문, 접속사 뒤 잘못된 쉼표라는 전형적 오개념으로 구성했다.

input.passage: In 1968, psychologists Robert Rosenthal and Lenore Jacobson told teachers at a California elementary school that certain students, identified by a new test, were poised for unusual intellectual growth. In fact, those students had been chosen at random. By year's end, the designated students, especially in the early grades, showed larger IQ gains than their classmates, a result widely cited as evidence that teacher expectations can become self-fulfilling. Later researchers, however, noted that the gains were concentrated among a small number of younger children and that some of the test scores were implausible, and attempts to replicate the original effect produced inconsistent results. Studies that instead observed teachers whose expectations formed naturally found that those expectations generally predicted student performance accurately rather than shaping it, with expectation effects typically modest in size. Even so, these studies identified groups, such as students from stigmatized backgrounds, for whom teacher expectations appeared to exert a stronger influence on achievement.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: A 1968 study showed that teachers' beliefs about students' potential reliably raise the intellectual performance of children across all grade levels.
Later research showed that teachers' expectations have no measurable effect on student performance because they simply reflect students' existing abilities.
Although a famous study suggested that teachers' beliefs strongly shape achievement, subsequent work indicates the influence is usually small, though it may be larger for certain students.
Researchers have found that students from stigmatized backgrounds are more likely than other students to be randomly selected for studies of teacher expectations.
input.explanation: 지문은 1968년 연구가 교사 기대의 자기충족 효과를 보여 준 것처럼 알려졌지만, 이후 연구에서 그 효과는 대체로 작았고 낙인찍힌 집단에서는 더 클 수 있다는 흐름이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 원래 연구의 주장만 담았고, 실제 효과도 저학년에 집중되었으므로 '모든 학년'이라는 표현이 틀렸다. B는 기대가 성적을 대체로 정확히 예측했다는 부분은 맞지만, 효과가 '전혀 없다'는 단정은 효과가 작다는 내용 및 특정 집단에서는 더 크다는 내용과 모순된다. D는 낙인찍힌 집단과 무작위 선정이라는 지문의 단어를 엉뚱하게 결합한 진술이다.
input.explanation_en: The text moves from a famous 1968 study that seemed to show strong self-fulfilling teacher expectations, to later research finding the effects are usually modest, to the note that they may be stronger for some groups, so C is correct. A repeats only the original claim, and "across all grade levels" is wrong because the gains were concentrated among younger children. B gets right that expectations often accurately predicted performance, but saying they have "no measurable effect" contradicts the text's description of modest effects and of stronger effects for some students. D wrongly combines two details from the text, stigmatized backgrounds and random selection, into a claim the text never makes.
input.design: Two-step judgment: the reader has to combine the original finding, the later qualification, and the final exception. A and B each fit part of the text, so you can only rule them out by comparing them with the whole passage.

input.passage: After the Civil War, many landowners in the American South had land but little cash, while many formerly enslaved people had labor but no land. Sharecropping linked these two groups: a family farmed a plot owned by someone else and gave the landowner a portion of the harvest, often one-half of the crop. Because payment depended on the size of the harvest, a bad season hurt both sides at once ______ a good season let both share in the gains.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.design: 독립절 두 개 사이에서 쉼표 스플라이스, 접속사 없이 붙인 문장(run-on), 접속사 뒤 쉼표 오용과 세미콜론+접속부사를 대비시켜 규칙 하나만 알면 풀 수 있게 했다.
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "a bad season hurt both sides at once"와 빈칸 뒤 "a good season let both share in the gains"는 각각 독립절이다. D는 세미콜론으로 두 독립절을 바르게 연결하고, 접속부사 similarly 뒤에 쉼표를 찍었으므로 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다. A는 등위접속사 but 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 찍었고, 두 절의 관계가 대조가 아니라 비슷한 결과이므로 but도 논리에 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("a bad season hurt both sides at once") and the words after it ("a good season let both share in the gains") are both independent clauses. D is correct because a semicolon can join two independent clauses, and the transition "similarly" is followed by a comma. B joins the two clauses with only a comma, so it creates a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, so it creates a run-on sentence. A puts an unneeded comma after the conjunction "but," and "but" also doesn't fit the logic, since the two clauses describe matching outcomes, not contrasting ones.

content.text: Easy 수준의 주어-동사 수 일치 문항: 짧은 수식어가 붙은 복수 주어.

input.passage: In sixteenth-century Italy, traveling troupes performed commedia dell'arte, a form of theater built on improvisation rather than fixed scripts. Actors relied on familiar stock characters, such as the greedy merchant Pantalone and the clever servant Arlecchino. The leather masks of these characters ______ each figure instantly recognizable to audiences, even in crowded town squares.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 주어는 복수 명사 'masks'이고 'of these characters'는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 동사는 복수 주어와 일치해야 하며, 과거형 C는 단수·복수 구분 없이 쓸 수 있어 수 일치 조건을 충족하고, 16세기를 다루는 지문의 과거 맥락과도 맞는다. A, B, D는 모두 단수 동사 형태(makes, is making, has made)라 복수 주어 'masks'와 수가 맞지 않는다. 바로 앞에 'characters'가 있지만 이는 전치사의 목적어이므로 동사의 수를 정하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of the sentence is the plural noun "masks." The phrase "of these characters" only modifies it. That means the verb has to agree with a plural subject. Choice C, the past tense "made," has the same form for singular and plural subjects, so it agrees with "masks." It also fits the sixteenth-century, past-tense setting of the passage. Choices A, B, and D are all singular forms ("makes," "is making," "has made"), so they don't agree with "masks." Don't let the nearby word "characters" fool you: it is the object of the preposition "of," so it doesn't control the verb.
input.design: 짧은 전치사구가 붙은 복수 주어로 수 일치 한 가지 규칙만 묻는다. 오답은 모두 단수 동사형이다.

input.passage: Naked mole rats live in underground colonies of up to several hundred individuals, yet typically only one female, the queen, breeds. For decades, researchers assumed she enforced this arrangement mainly through chemical signals released in her urine, as happens in some insect colonies. Biologist Melissa Holmes and colleagues tested this idea by exposing nonbreeding females to bedding soaked with the queen's urine, and they found that the females' reproductive hormones did not drop as predicted. Instead, the team observed that the queen regularly shoves and nudges other colony members as she patrols the tunnels, and that females removed from her physical presence began to mature sexually within weeks, even when they could still smell her. The researchers concluded that the queen's suppression of breeding depends far more on direct bodily contact than on scent.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Research suggests that a naked mole rat queen keeps other females from breeding chiefly through physical interaction rather than through chemical cues.
Research suggests that a naked mole rat queen keeps other females from breeding chiefly through chemical cues, much as queens in some insect colonies do.
Research suggests that nonbreeding naked mole rat females mature sexually only after the queen of their colony has died.
Research suggests that naked mole rat colonies grow larger when the queen spends more time patrolling the tunnels.
input.explanation: 지문은 여왕이 소변 속 화학 신호로 번식을 억제한다는 기존 가정을 소개한 뒤, 실험으로 이를 반박하고 직접적인 신체 접촉이 핵심이라고 결론짓는다. 그래서 A가 정답이다. B는 지문에 나오는 기존 가정을 그대로 옮긴 것인데, 지문은 바로 이 가정을 반박한다. C는 성숙이 여왕과 떨어졌을 때 일어났다는 세부를 여왕의 죽음으로 잘못 바꿨다. D는 순찰이라는 세부를 쓰지만 군집 크기와의 관계는 지문에서 다루지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The text first describes the old assumption that the queen suppresses breeding with chemical signals in her urine. It then explains how experiments contradicted that idea and concludes that direct bodily contact matters most, so A is correct. B repeats the old assumption, which the text rejects. C distorts a detail: females matured when they were separated from the queen, not after she died. D uses the patrolling detail, but the text never links patrolling to colony size.
input.design: 이 문항은 두 단계를 거쳐야 풀린다. 먼저 기존 가정을 파악하고, 이어서 그 가정이 반박된다는 점을 연결해야 한다. 지문을 훑어 읽으면 urine/insect 같은 표면 단서 때문에 B를 고르기 쉽다. C와 D는 지문의 세부(분리, 순찰)를 잘못 확장해 만들었고, 네 선택지는 같은 문장 틀로 썼다.

input.passage: In The Great Transformation (1944), economic historian Karl Polanyi argued that in most societies before the nineteenth century, economic activity was "embedded" in social relationships: goods moved through kinship obligations, religious duties, or reciprocal gift exchange, and prices were constrained by custom. Industrial capitalism, he claimed, tried to "disembed" the economy, treating land, labor, and money as commodities governed only by supply and demand. Some anthropologists have since challenged the sharpness of this contrast. Studying present-day commodity traders in Chicago and wholesale fish markets in Tokyo, they found that deals often depend on long-standing personal trust, reputations kept within tight circles, and informal norms about who may trade with whom, and that these factors sometimes outweigh price in deciding a sale. If these findings are representative, they suggest that ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: Polanyi was mistaken in claiming that economic activity in pre-nineteenth-century societies was shaped by kinship and custom.
Polanyi may have overstated how completely industrial capitalism separated economic exchange from social ties.
Polanyi was correct that modern markets operate on supply and demand alone, but only outside major financial centers.
Polanyi underestimated how strongly price determined exchanges in societies before the nineteenth century.
input.explanation: 지문은 폴라니가 산업 자본주의가 경제를 사회관계에서 '분리'했다고 주장했지만, 현대 시카고·도쿄 시장에서도 신뢰·평판·비공식 규범이 거래를 좌우한다는 인류학 연구를 제시한다. 따라서 현대 시장의 분리 정도를 과장했을 수 있다는 B가 결론이다. A는 연구가 산업화 이전 사회가 아닌 현대 시장을 다루므로 틀리다. C는 주요 금융 중심지에서조차 사회적 요인이 작용한다는 증거와 정반대다. D는 산업화 이전 사회에 대한 증거가 지문에 없어 근거가 없다.
input.explanation_en: The passage says Polanyi believed industrial capitalism "disembedded" the economy from social relationships, but anthropologists found that trust, reputation, and informal norms still shape deals in modern markets in Chicago and Tokyo. That evidence suggests the separation was less complete than Polanyi claimed, so B is correct. A is wrong because the studies looked at modern markets, not pre-nineteenth-century societies. C contradicts the evidence, since the social factors showed up in major financial centers themselves. D makes a claim about earlier societies that the new research never addresses.
input.design: Two steps: identify which half of Polanyi's contrast (modern disembedding) the modern-market evidence targets, then match the strength of the conclusion. The distractors misplace the critique (A, D) or reverse it (C).

input.passage: In the 1960s and 1970s, British sociologist Basil Bernstein proposed that children learn to speak in different "codes" depending on how their families communicate. A restricted code relies on meanings shared by speakers who know one another well, so much can go unsaid; an elaborated code spells out meanings explicitly so that strangers can follow them. Bernstein observed that working-class children tended to use mostly restricted codes, while middle-class children moved easily between both. Critics later accused him of claiming that working-class speech was deficient, but Bernstein rejected that reading. Restricted codes, he insisted, are rich and efficient within close-knit groups. His concern was with schools, which reward the elaborated code almost exclusively in their lessons, tests, and judgments of ability. Because some children arrive already fluent in that code and others do not, he argued, schools end up treating a difference in communication style as a difference in intelligence, reproducing the class inequalities they claim to reduce.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Bernstein found that working-class children use restricted codes because their families communicate less often than middle-class families do.
Bernstein argued that restricted codes are more efficient than elaborated codes and should therefore replace them in classroom instruction.
Bernstein's critics showed that his theory of linguistic codes unfairly ranked working-class speech below middle-class speech.
Bernstein held that schools deepen class inequality by favoring one communication style and mistaking unfamiliarity with it for lower ability.
input.explanation: 글은 비판자들의 오해를 소개한 뒤 Bernstein의 진짜 관심사를 제시한다. 학교가 elaborated code만 보상하기 때문에 의사소통 방식의 차이를 지능의 차이로 취급하고, 그 결과 계층 불평등을 재생산한다는 것이며, 이를 정확히 요약한 것이 D다. A는 계층과 코드의 연관성은 맞지만, 가정이 대화를 덜 한다는 내용은 글에 없다. B는 restricted code가 효율적이라는 부분은 맞지만, 교실에서 이를 대체해야 한다는 주장은 Bernstein이 한 적이 없다. C는 비판자들의 주장을 사실로 다루고 있지만, 글에서 Bernstein은 그런 해석을 거부했다.
input.explanation_en: The text brings up the critics' misreading and then states what Bernstein actually cared about. Because schools reward only the elaborated code, they treat a difference in communication style as a difference in intelligence, and this reproduces class inequality. Choice D sums that up correctly. Choice A gets the link between class and code right, but the text never says working-class families talk less. Choice B is right that restricted codes are efficient, but Bernstein never said they should replace elaborated codes in classrooms. Choice C presents the critics' charge as fact, while the text says Bernstein rejected that reading.
input.design: Bernstein의 진짜 주장은 비판에 대한 반박 뒤에야 나오도록 지문을 짰다. 그래서 훑어 읽으면 A, B, C처럼 지문 일부만 근거로 한 선택지에 끌리게 된다.

input.passage: Kintsugi is a Japanese method of repairing broken pottery with lacquer mixed with powdered gold. Instead of hiding the cracks, the repair makes them shine across the surface of the bowl or ______ the object's history becomes part of its beauty. This approach reflects wabi-sabi, an aesthetic that finds value in imperfection and change.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "the repair makes them shine ... cup"과 뒤 "the object's history becomes part of its beauty"는 각각 독립절이므로 둘을 제대로 분리해야 한다. B는 마침표로 두 문장을 나누고 "In this way," 뒤에 쉼표를 넣어 올바르다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이은 쉼표 스플라이스이다. C는 두 독립절 사이에 아무 문장부호가 없는 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 "and"로 잇기는 하지만 "in this way" 뒤에 쉼표가 없어 "this way the object's history"처럼 읽혀 혼동을 주므로, 표준 정답으로는 B가 가장 적절하다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("the repair makes them shine ... cup") and the text after it ("the object's history becomes part of its beauty") are both independent clauses, so they need a proper boundary between them. B separates them with a period and puts a comma after the introductory phrase "In this way," which is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C has no punctuation at all between the clauses, so it's a run-on sentence. D adds "and," but it leaves out the comma after "in this way," so the phrase runs into the next clause and reads awkwardly. That makes B the best choice.
input.design: Two clearly visible independent clauses; distractors are comma splice, fused sentence, and a conjunction variant missing the introductory-phrase comma.

input.passage: Between 1899 and 1901, members of a secret society known in English as the Boxers attacked foreign missionaries and Chinese Christians across northern China. The uprising grew out of anger at foreign powers that had gained control over Chinese ports and trade ______ many Boxers also blamed these outsiders for droughts and economic hardship in their villages.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.design: 독립절 두 개가 접속사 없이 이어지는 경계로, 세미콜론만 맞고 쉼표 스플라이스·무부호 연결·잘못된 쉼표 배치가 오답이다.
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The uprising grew ... trade"와 빈칸 뒤 "many Boxers also blamed ..."는 각각 독립절이다. 접속사 없이 두 독립절을 이으려면 세미콜론이 필요하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 아무 부호 없이 이어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 접속사 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 문장 흐름을 부적절하게 끊는다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("The uprising grew ... trade") and the text after it ("many Boxers also blamed ...") are both independent clauses. When you join two independent clauses without a conjunction, you need a semicolon, so B is correct. A uses only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence. D puts an unnecessary comma after the conjunction "and," which breaks up the sentence incorrectly.

input.passage: In a well-known social psychology study, college students were asked to wear a T-shirt showing a famous singer's face into a room full of peers. Afterward, the students guessed that about half of the people in the room had noticed the shirt. In reality, only about a quarter of the observers could recall it ______ researchers call this mistaken belief that others are paying close attention to us the spotlight effect.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "In reality, only about a quarter of the observers could recall it"와 뒤 "researchers call this ... the spotlight effect"는 각각 독립절이므로, 마침표로 두 문장을 나눈 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 접속사 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 and와 뒤 절을 부자연스럽게 끊어 놓는다.
input.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("In reality, only about a quarter of the observers could recall it") form an independent clause, and so do the words after it ("researchers call this ... the spotlight effect"). Choice A is correct because a period properly separates them into two sentences. Choice B joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, so it creates a comma splice. Choice C puts no punctuation between the two clauses, so it creates a run-on sentence. Choice D adds an unneeded comma right after the conjunction "and," which wrongly cuts "and" off from the clause it introduces.
input.design: 절 경계가 명확한 두 독립절 사이의 마침표 선택 문제로, 쉼표 스플라이스·무종지문·접속사 뒤 쉼표라는 전형적 오개념을 오답으로 배치했다.

content.text:
Easy subject-verb agreement with short modifier.

Passage: "In 1887, Ludwik Zamenhof published a short booklet introducing Esperanto, a language he hoped would serve as a neutral bridge between speakers of different native tongues. Today, the grammar of Esperanto ______ only sixteen basic rules, which learners can master in a few weeks."

Subject "grammar" singular → "contains". Options: contain, are containing, have contained, contains. Don't repeat "Esperanto" — fine. Question is fixed wording, okay.

input.passage: In 1887, Ludwik Zamenhof published a short booklet introducing Esperanto, a constructed language he hoped would serve as a neutral bridge between speakers of different native tongues. Today, the grammar of Esperanto ______ only sixteen basic rules, so many learners can master its structure within a few weeks.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 동사의 주어는 단수 명사 'grammar'이고, 'of Esperanto'는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 현재형 동사인 D 'contains'가 정답이다. A는 복수 주어에 쓰는 형태라 단수 주어 'grammar'와 맞지 않는다. B의 'are'와 C의 'have'도 복수 주어용이라 수 일치에 어긋난다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of the blank is the singular noun "grammar." The phrase "of Esperanto" just describes that subject, so it doesn't change the number. That's why D, "contains," is correct: it's a singular present-tense verb. A is the form used with plural subjects, so it doesn't agree with "grammar." B ("are") and C ("have") also go with plural subjects, so they break subject-verb agreement too.
input.design: This item tests one rule: subject-verb agreement with a singular subject followed by a short prepositional modifier. The clue "Today" points to present tense, and all three wrong answers use the plural form.

input.passage: Leatherback sea turtles cross entire ocean basins, and researchers have long suspected that the turtles navigate partly by sensing Earth's magnetic field, whose intensity and inclination angle vary predictably across the globe. To test this, a team placed young leatherbacks in a tank surrounded by electric coils that could reproduce the magnetic conditions of specific ocean locations. When the coils mimicked the field found off the turtles' natal beaches in the Caribbean, the turtles swam in no consistent direction. But when the coils reproduced the field of a site far to the northeast, near the edge of the North Atlantic current system, the turtles consistently oriented toward the southwest—the direction that would carry them back toward their usual migratory loop. Notably, the turtles had never traveled to that northeastern site. These findings suggest that ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: young leatherbacks learn the magnetic signatures of distant ocean sites by remembering fields they encountered during earlier stages of their migration.
young leatherbacks rely mainly on the magnetic field of their natal beaches, which allows them to swim directly back toward the Caribbean from anywhere.
young leatherbacks can sense the strength of a magnetic field but are unable to use that information to choose a direction of travel.
young leatherbacks respond to certain regional magnetic conditions with an appropriate heading even before they have any firsthand experience of those regions.
input.explanation: 거북들은 한 번도 가 본 적 없는 북동쪽 지점의 자기장에 대해 이동 경로로 돌아가는 남서쪽 방향을 일관되게 택했으므로, 경험 없이도 특정 자기 조건에 알맞은 방향으로 반응한다는 D가 정답이다. A는 자기 신호를 학습한다는 설명이지만, 해당 지점에 가 본 적이 없다는 진술과 모순된다. B는 출생 해변 자기장을 강조하지만, 그 자기장에서는 거북들이 일정한 방향 없이 헤엄쳤다. C는 자기장 감지는 인정하지만, 거북들이 방향을 일관되게 정했다는 결과와 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The turtles had never visited the northeastern site, yet when they were exposed to its magnetic field, they consistently headed southwest, back toward their migratory loop. That's why D is the answer: the turtles responded to a regional field with a suitable heading without any firsthand experience. A says the turtles learned these signatures from earlier travel, but the text states that they had never been to that site. B focuses on the natal-beach field, but under that field the turtles swam in no consistent direction. C admits the turtles can sense the field but says they can't use it to choose a direction, which goes against their consistent southwest heading.
input.design: To answer, students must connect two pieces of information: the consistent southwest heading and the fact that the turtles had never been to the site. A sounds plausible because it mentions navigation, and B uses the natal-beach detail, so careful comparison is needed to rule them out.

input.passage: When ultraviolet light strikes particles of titanium dioxide, a common semiconductor, it can push electrons across the material's bandgap and leave positively charged "holes" behind. These holes react with water molecules to form hydroxyl ______ the radicals then break apart dyes and other pollutants dissolved in wastewater.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "These holes react with water molecules to form hydroxyl radicals"와 뒤 "the radicals then break apart dyes..."는 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 접속사 없이 두 독립절을 이으려면 세미콜론이 필요하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 문장부호가 전혀 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D의 "then"은 등위접속사가 아니라 부사라서 쉼표와 함께 써도 여전히 쉼표 스플라이스이다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("These holes react with water molecules to form hydroxyl radicals") and the text after it ("the radicals then break apart dyes...") are both independent clauses, since each has its own subject and verb. When you join two independent clauses without a conjunction, you need a semicolon, so B is correct. A joins the clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C has no punctuation at all, so it creates a run-on sentence. D adds "then," but "then" is an adverb, not a coordinating conjunction, so the comma before it still makes a comma splice.
input.design: 빈칸 양쪽 모두 주어와 동사가 분명한 짧은 독립절이라 한 가지 규칙(접속사 없는 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결)만 알면 풀린다. 오답은 흔한 오개념인 쉼표 스플라이스, 무종지문, 부사 then을 접속사로 착각하는 경우로 구성했다.

input.passage: Russian painter Wassily Kandinsky believed that colors could be heard as well as seen. In his 1911 book Concerning the Spiritual in Art, he linked yellow to the sharp blast of a trumpet and deep blue to the low tones of a cello. These ideas shaped his abstract canvases, which he often titled "Compositions" as if they were pieces of ______ wanted viewers to experience his paintings the way listeners experience a symphony.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "These ideas shaped ... pieces of music"과 뒤의 "Kandinsky wanted viewers ..."는 각각 독립절이므로 마침표로 분리해야 한다. 그래서 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 이어 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 등위접속사 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표가 들어가 문장부호 사용이 잘못되었다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("These ideas shaped ... pieces of music") and the text after it ("Kandinsky wanted viewers ...") are both independent clauses, so they need to be separated with a period. That makes A correct. B joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C runs the clauses together with no punctuation at all, creating a run-on sentence. D adds an extra comma after the coordinating conjunction "and," and that comma doesn't belong there.
input.design: 독립절 두 개의 경계가 분명한 쉬운 문항으로, 쉼표 스플라이스·무종지문·잘못된 쉼표 같은 전형적 오개념을 오답으로 배치했다.

input.passage: Historians have long debated whether the militant tactics of Britain's Women's Social and Political Union (WSPU), founded in 1903, advanced or hindered the cause of women's suffrage. Some argue that window smashing and arson alienated members of Parliament who might otherwise have supported reform. Yet historian June Purvis notes that before the WSPU's campaigns, suffrage bills were routinely introduced and quietly allowed to lapse, attracting little press coverage. After militancy began, newspapers reported on suffrage almost daily, and party leaders could no longer treat the question as marginal. Purvis concedes that militancy did not by itself secure the 1918 and 1928 acts, which followed wartime shifts in public opinion. Taken together, these points suggest that militancy's main contribution was ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: persuading members of Parliament who had opposed reform to vote for the suffrage bills that were introduced before 1914.
producing the shift in public opinion during the war that led directly to the passage of the 1918 and 1928 acts.
preventing the suffrage question from receiving serious attention by alienating potential supporters in Parliament.
making women's suffrage a prominent political issue, even though other factors were needed to achieve the vote itself.
input.explanation: Purvis는 투쟁 전술 이후 언론 보도가 늘고 정당 지도자들이 참정권 문제를 무시할 수 없게 되었다고 말하면서도, 투쟁만으로 1918년·1928년 법이 통과된 것은 아니라고 인정한다. 이 두 정보를 연결하면 D가 정답이다. A는 반대 의원들이 실제로 찬성표를 던졌다는 근거가 지문에 없다. B는 전시 여론 변화를 투쟁의 결과로 보는데, 지문은 이를 별개의 요인으로 제시한다. C는 일부 역사가의 견해일 뿐, Purvis의 근거는 오히려 관심이 커졌음을 보여 준다.
input.explanation_en: Purvis points out that after militancy began, the press covered suffrage almost daily and party leaders couldn't treat it as marginal anymore. She also admits that militancy alone didn't win the 1918 and 1928 acts. If you put those two points together, you get D. A is wrong because the text never says opponents changed their votes. B is wrong because it treats the wartime shift in opinion as something militancy caused, but the text presents it as a separate factor. C repeats the critics' view, and Purvis's evidence actually shows that attention to the issue grew.
input.design: To get this right, students have to link two pieces of Purvis's argument: militancy made the issue prominent, and she concedes it didn't win the vote on its own. Each distractor latches onto one partial clue from the text: the critics' view, wartime opinion, or Parliament.

input.passage: In the 1970s, chemists Mario Molina and F. Sherwood Rowland warned that chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), once common in spray cans and refrigerators, could drift into the stratosphere and break apart under strong sunlight. The chlorine released by this breakdown destroys ozone molecules ______ the thinning is most severe over Antarctica each spring, when returning sunlight triggers the chemical reactions that allow more ultraviolet radiation to reach the surface.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The chlorine ... destroys ozone molecules at a rapid rate"와 빈칸 뒤 "the thinning is most severe ..."는 각각 독립절이다. 접속사 없이 두 독립절을 잇는 데는 세미콜론이 적절하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 아무 부호 없이 이어 run-on 문장이 된다. C는 "and" 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 "and"와 다음 절의 주어 사이를 끊는다.
input.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("The chlorine ... destroys ozone molecules at a rapid rate") form an independent clause, and so do the words after it ("the thinning is most severe ..."). When two independent clauses are joined without a conjunction, a semicolon is correct, so D is the answer. A joins the clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B uses no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. C puts an extra comma after "and," which cuts "and" off from the subject of the next clause for no reason.
input.design: 쉬운 난이도로, 두 독립절의 경계가 바로 보이게 만들었다. 오답은 쉼표 스플라이스, 아무 부호 없이 이어 쓴 run-on, 접속사 뒤 불필요한 쉼표라는 흔한 실수로 구성했다.

input.passage: Mantis shrimp are often celebrated for having twelve or more types of color photoreceptors, compared with the three found in humans, and many popular accounts assume this gives them extraordinarily rich color vision. In 2014, however, biologist Hanne Thoen and colleagues trained mantis shrimp to pick out specific wavelengths and found that the animals were surprisingly poor at telling apart colors that humans distinguish easily. The researchers proposed that, rather than comparing signals across receptor types as human eyes do, mantis shrimp may recognize colors directly from which single receptor responds most strongly, a method that sacrifices fine discrimination for speed. This interpretation fits with other features of their visual system, such as their ability to detect circularly polarized light, which suggests that their eyes are tuned for rapidly reading particular signals rather than for perceiving subtle gradations.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Mantis shrimp have more types of color photoreceptors than humans do, which allows them to distinguish subtle shades of color more precisely than humans can.
Mantis shrimp's many photoreceptor types may support fast identification of colors rather than fine discrimination, contrary to a common assumption about their vision.
Mantis shrimp's ability to detect circularly polarized light is more important to their survival than their ability to perceive color.
Mantis shrimp compare signals across several receptor types at once, which explains why they struggled in a wavelength-discrimination experiment.
input.explanation: 지문은 광수용체가 많으면 색 구분이 뛰어날 것이라는 통념을 소개한 뒤, 실험 결과 구분 능력이 낮았고 대신 빠른 색 인식에 맞춰진 것일 수 있다고 주장하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 첫 문장의 통념을 그대로 옮긴 것으로, 지문이 반박하는 내용이다. C는 편광 감지를 언급하지만 지문은 그것을 해석을 뒷받침하는 근거로만 쓸 뿐 생존상 중요도를 비교하지 않는다. D는 실험 결과는 맞게 말하지만, 여러 수용체의 신호를 비교하는 것은 인간의 방식이고 갯가재는 가장 강하게 반응하는 단일 수용체를 쓴다고 했으므로 원인을 거꾸로 설명한다.
input.explanation_en: The text starts with the popular belief that more photoreceptors means richer color vision. It then describes an experiment showing the shrimp discriminate colors poorly and suggests their system is built for quick recognition instead, so B is correct. A just repeats the popular assumption that the text goes on to challenge. C brings up polarization, but the text uses polarization only as supporting evidence and never says it matters more for survival than color vision. D gets the experimental result right but has the mechanism backward: comparing signals across receptor types is what human eyes do, while mantis shrimp may rely on whichever single receptor responds most strongly.
input.design: To pick the right answer, you have to connect the common assumption, the experimental result, and the proposed mechanism. A and D each borrow true details from the text but either restate the assumption the text rejects or flip the mechanism.

input.passage: Sociologist Pierre Bourdieu argued that schools, though officially neutral, reward a kind of "cultural capital"—familiarity with canonical art, literature, and ways of speaking about them—that children from affluent families typically absorb at home rather than learn in class. To test this idea, a research team compared students who scored equally well on a test of formally taught material, such as grammar rules and historical dates. Despite these identical scores, students whose parents frequently took them to museums and concerts received noticeably higher grades from teachers on open-ended essays about artworks, and these grades were linked to the students' relaxed, confident manner of discussing the works rather than to accuracy. If Bourdieu is correct, these findings suggest that ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: teachers' assessments may partly reward a style of engagement acquired outside school, allowing family advantages to appear as individual academic merit.
students from affluent families learn formally taught material more thoroughly than other students do, which explains their higher essay grades.
museum and concert visits improve students' factual knowledge of art history, which teachers then reward with higher grades on essays.
open-ended essays are a less reliable measure of achievement than tests of formal material, so schools should replace essays with such tests.
input.design: 두 정보(형식적 시험 점수는 같음 + 에세이 점수 차이는 정확성이 아닌 태도에서 옴)를 연결해야 하며, B·C는 '점수 차이'라는 부분적 근거를 지문과 맞지 않는 원인과 엮었고, D는 그럴듯하지만 지문 범위를 넘는 처방이다.
input.explanation: 두 집단은 학교에서 가르친 내용의 시험 점수가 같았고, 에세이 점수 차이는 정확성이 아니라 여유롭고 자신감 있는 말하기 방식과 관련이 있었습니다. 이는 집에서 습득한 문화자본이 개인의 실력처럼 보상된다는 부르디외의 주장과 맞아떨어지므로 A가 정답입니다. B는 형식적 학습 내용 점수가 같았다는 사실과 모순됩니다. C는 점수 차이를 사실 지식 덕분으로 보지만, 지문은 점수가 정확성과는 관련이 없었다고 말합니다. D는 지문이 다루지 않은 정책 권고까지 나아간 것으로, 연구 결과를 넘어서는 결론입니다.
input.explanation_en: The two groups scored the same on formally taught material, and the gap in essay grades was linked to a relaxed, confident manner, not to accuracy. That fits Bourdieu's claim that cultural capital picked up at home gets rewarded as if it were individual merit, so A is correct. B contradicts the identical scores on formally taught material. C credits the gap to factual knowledge, but the passage says the grades weren't tied to accuracy. D jumps to a policy recommendation the passage never discusses, so it goes beyond what the findings support.

content.text:
Passage: Thermal paste. Two independent clauses with comma splice.

"Even surfaces that look perfectly flat contain microscopic gaps that trap air, a poor conductor of heat. Thermal paste fills these gaps between a CPU and its heatsink______ applying too thick a layer, however, can actually slow heat transfer."

Hmm, "however" complicates. Simpler: "Thermal paste fills tiny air gaps between a computer chip and its heatsink______ the paste conducts heat far better than the trapped air it replaces."

Options: A ", the paste" comma splice — but cannot repeat word before blank; blank is after "heatsink", options start with punctuation, fine. Options: A ", the" ... Better keep options punctuation only: A ", " B "" (no punctuation)— blank option tricky. Use: A ", the paste conducts", B " the paste conducts", C "; the paste conducts", D ", conducting the paste"? Keep same frame: A ", the paste" B "the paste" (run-on) C "; the paste" D ", and, the paste" hmm. D ": and the paste"? Let's do D ", so, the paste"? Better D "and, the paste" — wrong comma. Fine.

input.passage: Even metal surfaces that look perfectly smooth are covered with tiny bumps and pits. When a computer chip is pressed against a heatsink, these flaws trap pockets of air, which slows the flow of heat away from the chip. Thermal paste solves this problem by filling the tiny gaps between the two surfaces______ the paste carries heat far better than the air it replaces.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Thermal paste solves ... surfaces"와 뒤 "the paste carries ... replaces"는 각각 완전한 독립절이다. 접속사 없이 두 독립절을 잇는 데에는 세미콜론이 적절하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 접속사 and 바로 뒤에 쉼표를 찍었는데, 두 절 사이의 이 위치에는 쉼표가 필요하지 않다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("Thermal paste solves ... surfaces") and the text after it ("the paste carries ... replaces") are both independent clauses. When there's no conjunction joining two independent clauses, a semicolon is the right way to connect them, so C is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B runs the two clauses together with no punctuation at all, so it's a run-on sentence. D puts a comma right after the conjunction "and," but no comma is needed in that spot between the two clauses.
input.design: Two plainly visible independent clauses; distractors are the classic comma splice, run-on, and misplaced comma after a conjunction, all built on the same "the paste" frame.

input.passage: The American pika, a small relative of rabbits, lives on rocky talus slopes in western North American mountains. Pikas do not hibernate and have a high resting body temperature, so they can die after only a few hours of exposure to air above about 25°C. In many mountain ranges, pika populations exist as isolated patches on separate peaks, divided by warm, low-elevation valleys. Ecologist researchers surveying the Great Basin found that pikas had disappeared from several lower-elevation sites where they had been recorded decades earlier, while populations on higher, cooler peaks generally persisted. Because a pika lost from one peak can be replaced only by individuals crossing the intervening valleys, the researchers concluded that as summers warm, ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: pikas on lower peaks will likely move down into the valleys, where food plants are more plentiful than on rocky talus slopes.
pikas on higher peaks will likely be the first to disappear, since those populations are the most isolated from other populations.
pikas that vanish from a peak are increasingly unlikely to be replaced, since the valleys separating peaks will become harder for pikas to cross.
pikas will likely grow less sensitive to heat over time, since the populations that have survived are found mostly on higher peaks.
input.explanation: 지문은 피카가 약 25°C 이상에서 몇 시간 만에 죽을 수 있다는 점, 그리고 한 봉우리의 개체군이 사라지면 따뜻한 계곡을 건너온 개체로만 다시 채워질 수 있다는 점을 제시한다. 이 두 정보를 연결하면, 여름이 따뜻해질수록 계곡을 건너기가 더 어려워져 사라진 개체군이 다시 채워질 가능성이 낮아진다는 결론이 나오므로 C가 정답이다. A는 먹이를 언급하지만, 지문은 따뜻한 저지대가 피카에게 치명적이라고 말한다. B는 고립을 언급하지만, 지문에서 높은 봉우리의 개체군은 대체로 살아남았다. D는 살아남은 개체군의 분포를 내열성의 진화로 잘못 해석하며, 지문은 이를 뒷받침하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The passage gives you two key facts: pikas can die after a few hours in air above about 25°C, and a peak that loses its pikas can be repopulated only by pikas crossing warm valleys. If you connect these facts, warmer summers make those crossings more dangerous, so lost populations become less likely to be replaced. That makes C the answer. A mentions food, but the passage says warm low elevations are deadly to pikas. B brings up isolation, but the passage says populations on higher peaks generally survived. D treats where the surviving pikas live as evidence that they are evolving heat tolerance, and nothing in the passage supports that.
input.design: To answer, students must combine the pika's heat limit with the way peaks get repopulated. Wrong answers B and D each use a real detail from the passage (isolation, survival on high peaks) but draw the wrong conclusion from it.

input.passage: When Tsar Alexander II issued his emancipation decree in 1861, roughly twenty-three million privately owned serfs in the Russian Empire gained personal freedom: they could marry, own property, and bring lawsuits without a landlord's permission. The land question was settled far less generously. Peasants received allotments, but these were often smaller than the plots they had farmed before, and the best meadows and woodlands frequently stayed with the nobility. Former serfs also had to pay "redemption payments" for their allotments over forty-nine years. In most regions the land went not to individual households but to the village commune, which periodically redistributed strips among families and was held collectively responsible for the payments. Historians therefore describe the reform as one that ended legal bondage while leaving many peasants economically tied to their villages and burdened by debt for decades.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The 1861 decree gave former serfs both personal freedom and enough land to farm independently, though the nobility kept control of meadows and woodlands.
Although the 1861 decree freed serfs in law, how it handled land kept many of them financially burdened and bound to their communities.
Although the 1861 decree created village communes to manage land, these communes mainly helped peasants avoid redemption payments to former landlords.
Although the 1861 decree affected some twenty-three million serfs, historians mainly value it for the new legal rights it gave peasants to marry and sue.
input.explanation: 지문은 1861년 칙령이 법적 예속은 끝냈지만, 작은 분배지·상환금·공동체 소유 때문에 농민이 경제적으로 묶이고 빚에 시달렸다는 대비를 중심으로 하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 귀족이 초지와 숲을 가졌다는 세부는 맞지만, 독립 경작에 충분한 토지를 받았다는 부분이 지문(이전보다 작은 분배지)과 어긋난다. C는 공동체가 토지를 관리했다는 점은 맞으나, 공동체는 오히려 상환금에 집단 책임을 졌으므로 납부를 피하게 도왔다는 진술은 틀렸다. D는 인원 수와 법적 권리라는 세부는 맞지만, 역사가들이 강조하는 점은 지속된 경제적 부담이므로 중심 내용을 잘못 짚었다.
input.explanation_en: The text sets up a contrast: the 1861 decree ended legal bondage, but small allotments, redemption payments, and commune ownership left many peasants tied to their villages and in debt, so B is correct. A gets right that the nobility kept meadows and woodlands, but the text says allotments were often smaller than before, not enough to farm independently. C correctly notes that communes managed the land, but they were held collectively responsible for the payments, so they did not help peasants avoid them. D uses accurate details (the number of serfs and the new legal rights), but historians focus on the lasting economic burden, so it misses the main point.
input.design: 각 오답에 지문의 맞는 세부(초지 보유, 공동체, 법적 권리)를 하나씩 넣고 결론이 틀리게 만들었다. 그래서 "자유 대 경제적 속박"이라는 대비를 이해하는지와 각 세부를 맞춰 보는 일, 이렇게 두 단계를 거쳐야 정답을 고를 수 있다.

content.text:
Passage: Early soft contact lenses were made of hydrogel, which carries oxygen to the cornea only through the water it holds. Silicone hydrogel lenses changed this ______ silicone lets far more oxygen pass through, so the risk of corneal hypoxia during overnight wear drops sharply.

Hmm, "changed this" plus a colon could also work. To keep it to one rule, I'll make it two independent clauses: "Silicone hydrogel lenses solved this problem in the late 1990s" + "their silicone component lets oxygen pass directly through the material." Options: comma splice ", their"; no punctuation "their"; comma + "and" wrongly placed? I need four options in the same frame: A ", their" (splice), B " their" (run-on), C "and, their" (error), D "; their" (correct). "Their" isn't the word before the blank, so that's fine.

input.passage: Early soft contact lenses were made of hydrogel, a material that delivers oxygen to the cornea only through the water it holds. When worn overnight, these lenses could starve the eye of oxygen, a condition called corneal hypoxia. Silicone hydrogel lenses, introduced in the late 1990s, largely solved this ______ silicone component lets oxygen pass directly through the lens material.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'Silicone hydrogel lenses ... largely solved this problem'과 뒤 'their silicone component lets oxygen pass ...'는 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. C는 접속사 and 뒤에 쉼표를 두어 문장부호 위치가 잘못되었다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("Silicone hydrogel lenses ... largely solved this problem") and the text after it ("their silicone component lets oxygen pass ...") are both independent clauses, each with its own subject and verb. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so D is correct. A joins them with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B puts no punctuation between them at all, which makes a run-on sentence. C puts the comma after "and" instead of before it, so the punctuation is in the wrong place.
input.design: This easy item uses one rule: two independent clauses with a clear boundary have to be joined with a semicolon. The wrong answers are common mistakes students make: a comma splice, a run-on, and a comma in the wrong place next to "and."

input.passage: Economist Keith Chen has studied whether the way a language marks the future affects how its speakers behave. English requires speakers to mark future events with words such as "will," while languages like Mandarin often let speakers describe the future using the present tense. Chen found that speakers of languages with weak future marking tended to save more ______ he suggested that talking about the future as if it were the present may make it feel closer.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Chen found ... save more money"와 뒤 "he suggested ... feel closer"는 각각 완전한 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D의 "then"은 등위접속사가 아닌 부사이므로 쉼표와 함께 써도 여전히 쉼표 스플라이스다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("Chen found ... save more money") and the text after it ("he suggested ... feel closer") are both independent clauses. A semicolon can correctly join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A joins them with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between them, which makes a run-on sentence. D adds "then," but "then" is an adverb, not a coordinating conjunction, so the result is still a comma splice.
input.design: 독립절 두 개 사이의 경계가 한눈에 보이도록 구성했고, 쉼표 스플라이스·무종지문·"then" 오개념을 오답으로 넣어 세미콜론 규칙 하나로 풀리게 했다.

input.passage: Afrofuturism is often described as a genre that imagines Black people in high-tech futures, and works such as Octavia Butler's novels or Sun Ra's cosmic jazz are frequently cited as examples. Some critics, however, argue that this description misses what many Afrofuturist artists are actually doing. In the work of contemporary painters and installation artists such as Wangechi Mutu and Cauleen Smith, futuristic imagery rarely appears on its own: spacecraft, cyborg bodies, and alien landscapes are combined with references to ancestral myths, the Middle Passage, and diasporic folk practices. For these artists, the critics contend, the future is less a destination than a way of reexamining the past, recovering histories that were erased or distorted so that they can shape new possibilities for the present.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Some critics contend that Afrofuturism is best defined by the novels of Octavia Butler and the music of Sun Ra rather than by contemporary visual art.
Some critics contend that contemporary Afrofuturist artists have abandoned futuristic imagery in favor of depicting ancestral myths and folk practices.
Some critics contend that Afrofuturist artists use images of technology chiefly to celebrate scientific progress within the Black diaspora.
Some critics contend that, for certain Afrofuturist artists, imagining the future serves mainly as a means of reclaiming and reinterpreting history.
input.explanation: 지문은 Afrofuturism을 단순히 첨단 미래 장르로 보는 시각을 비평가들이 반박하며, Mutu·Smith 같은 작가에게 미래는 지워진 과거를 되찾고 재해석하는 수단이라고 주장한다는 내용이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 Butler와 Sun Ra가 언급되긴 하지만 그것은 통념의 예시일 뿐이며, 비평가들이 이를 정의의 기준으로 삼는다는 내용은 없다. B는 조상 신화가 등장한다는 부분은 맞지만, 미래적 이미지를 버린 것이 아니라 과거와 '결합'한다고 했으므로 틀리다. C는 기술 이미지를 언급하지만 과학 진보의 찬양이라는 목적은 지문에 없다.
input.explanation_en: The text says critics reject the view of Afrofuturism as simply imagining high-tech futures, and argue that for artists like Mutu and Smith the future is a way to recover and reexamine erased histories, so D is correct. A goes wrong because Butler and Sun Ra appear only as examples of the common description, and the critics never treat them as the defining standard. B gets the ancestral myths right, but the artists combine futuristic imagery with the past instead of giving it up. C mentions technology imagery, but the text never says it is used to celebrate scientific progress.
input.design: 오답 A·B가 지문 세부(작가 예시, 신화 요소)를 부분적으로 활용해 결합/대체, 통념/주장 구분을 정독해야 배제되게 했고, 모든 선택지를 동일한 'Some critics contend that' 틀로 작성했다.

input.passage: When certain crystals such as quartz are crushed or ground, they briefly give off flashes of light, a phenomenon called triboluminescence. The stress of grinding breaks bonds in the crystal lattice and separates electric charges along fresh cracks. These charges quickly recombine across the tiny gaps, and the energy they release ______ some engineers now study the flashes to monitor how evenly minerals are being ground in industrial mills.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: "the energy they release appears as visible light"는 독립절이고, "some engineers now study..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. A는 마침표로 두 독립절을 나누고 "Today,"로 새 문장을 시작하므로 올바르다. B와 D는 접속사 없이 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 "today" 뒤에 쉼표만 있어서 역시 두 독립절이 쉼표로만 연결된다.
input.explanation_en: "The energy they release appears as visible light" is an independent clause, and "some engineers now study..." is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb. Choice A puts a period between the two clauses and starts a new sentence with "Today," so it is correct. Choices B and D join the two independent clauses with only a comma and no conjunction, which makes a comma splice. Choice C also links the clauses with nothing but the comma after "today," so it is a comma splice too.
input.design: 독립절 두 개가 만나는 경계 하나만 판단하면 되도록 만들었다. 오답은 모두 쉼표 스플라이스이고, "today"의 위치만 바꿔서 그럴듯해 보이게 했다.

input.passage: When the French effort to build a canal across Panama collapsed in 1889, observers often blamed engineering: Ferdinand de Lesseps had insisted on a sea-level channel, which required removing staggering volumes of earth. Yet the French had also lost more than 20,000 workers, chiefly to yellow fever and malaria, and labor shortages repeatedly halted excavation. When the United States took over in 1904, it adopted a lock-based design that reduced digging, but it also funded William Gorgas's campaign to drain standing water and screen buildings against mosquitoes, which eliminated yellow fever from the Canal Zone by 1906. Historians who note that American excavation accelerated sharply only after 1906, even though the lock design had been chosen earlier, suggest that ______
input.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the lock design, rather than disease control, was the main reason the American project succeeded where the French one had failed.
the French project would have been completed if de Lesseps had adopted a lock-based design from the beginning.
the American success depended at least as much on protecting workers from disease as on changing the canal's design.
yellow fever posed a smaller threat to canal workers than malaria did during the American construction period.
input.explanation: 락 설계는 1906년 이전에 채택됐지만 굴착이 급격히 빨라진 것은 황열병이 제거된 1906년 이후이므로, 성공에는 질병 통제가 설계 변경만큼 중요했다는 C가 정답이다. A는 설계 변경도 기여했다는 점에서 일부 맞지만, 시점 근거와 정반대 결론이다. B는 프랑스의 설계 문제를 언급한 점은 맞지만, 질병으로 인한 노동력 부족을 무시하고 지나치게 단정한다. D는 지문에서 두 질병의 위협 정도를 비교한 근거가 없다.
input.explanation_en: The lock design was chosen before 1906, but excavation sped up sharply only after yellow fever was eliminated in 1906. That timing shows disease control mattered at least as much as the design change, so C is correct. A is partly right, since the design did help, but it reaches the opposite of what the timing suggests. B picks up on the French design problems but ignores the disease-driven labor shortages and claims far too much. D compares the two diseases, and the passage gives no basis for that comparison.
input.design: To answer, you have to connect two facts: the design was adopted early, and the speedup came only after the 1906 disease control. The wrong answers about design (A, B) are tempting if you only skim.

input.passage: The Pacific lamprey is a jawless fish that feeds by attaching to a host fish with its round, sucker-like mouth disc. Once it is firmly attached, the lamprey uses rows of sharp teeth to scrape through the host's skin ______ its saliva contains chemicals that keep the host's blood from clotting while the lamprey feeds.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "the lamprey uses ... skin"과 빈칸 뒤 "its saliva contains ... feeds"는 각각 독립절이다. B는 마침표로 두 독립절을 분리하고 부사 Meanwhile 뒤에 쉼표를 두어 올바르다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 잇는 쉼표 스플라이스이다. C는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 런온 문장이다. D는 meanwhile이 접속사가 아닌 부사이므로 쉼표+meanwhile 역시 쉼표 스플라이스이다.
input.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("the lamprey uses ... skin") and the words after it ("its saliva contains ... feeds") are both independent clauses. B is correct because the period separates the two clauses, and the comma after the adverb "Meanwhile" is correct too. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C has no punctuation between the clauses at all, so it is a run-on sentence. D is also a comma splice, because "meanwhile" is an adverb, not a conjunction, so it can't join two clauses with just a comma.
input.design: 절 경계가 명확한 두 독립절 사이에서 마침표+접속부사 하나의 규칙만으로 풀게 하고, 오답은 쉼표 스플라이스·런온·접속부사 오용이라는 흔한 실수로 구성했다.

input.passage: In 1915, Ottoman authorities began removing Armenians from towns across Anatolia, ordering entire communities to march toward the Syrian desert. Officials often described these orders as wartime relocations meant to protect the empire from a supposedly disloyal population. Historians who have studied the period, however, point out that the deportations reached Armenians living far from any battlefront, that men were frequently separated and killed before the marches began, and that the routes and conditions made survival unlikely. Taken together, these patterns suggest that the removals were not a security measure that went tragically wrong but a coordinated effort to eliminate the Armenian population. Many scholars connect this effort to a Turkish nationalist ideology, increasingly influential among leaders of the ruling Committee of Union and Progress, that envisioned Anatolia as a homeland for one people, with no place for a large Christian minority.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Evidence about how the 1915 deportations were carried out indicates that they were a deliberate campaign of destruction rooted in nationalist aims, despite being presented as wartime relocations.
Evidence about how the 1915 deportations were carried out indicates that Ottoman officials mainly feared Armenian cooperation with enemy armies near the empire's borders.
Evidence about how the 1915 deportations were carried out indicates that harsh desert conditions, rather than official policy, caused most of the deaths among Armenians.
Evidence about how the 1915 deportations were carried out indicates that historians still disagree about whether nationalist ideology influenced Ottoman leaders at all.
input.explanation: 이 글은 강제 이주가 공식적으로는 전시 이주라고 설명되었지만, 실제로 어떻게 실행되었는지(전선과 먼 지역까지 포함, 남성 살해, 살아남기 어려운 경로)를 보면 의도적인 말살이었다고 주장하며, 그 배경을 민족주의 이념에 연결한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 관리들이 내세운 명분을 사실처럼 받아들인 것이고, 글은 오히려 전선과 먼 지역까지 이주가 이뤄졌다는 점을 들어 그 명분을 반박한다. C는 사막의 환경을 언급하긴 하지만, 글은 그런 조건이 계획의 일부였다고 보므로 정책이 아니었다는 주장과 맞지 않는다. D는 글에서 많은 학자가 이념과 연결한다고 한 내용과 어긋난다.
input.explanation_en: The text says the deportations were officially called wartime relocations. It then argues that the way they were carried out shows a deliberate effort to destroy the Armenian population: the orders reached areas far from any front, men were killed, and the routes made survival unlikely. It also links this effort to nationalist ideology, so A is correct. B treats the officials' stated reason as the truth, but the text actually undercuts that reason by pointing to deportations far from the battlefront. C mentions the desert conditions, but the text treats those conditions as part of the plan, not as something separate from official policy. D contradicts the text, which says many scholars connect the killings to nationalist ideology.
input.design: All four options use the same sentence frame, and each wrong choice borrows a real detail from the text (security claims, desert routes, scholars). To rule them out, students have to connect the evidence the text gives with its conclusion that the killings were deliberate and driven by ideology.

input.passage: In the late thirteenth century, the Majorcan philosopher Ramon Llull devised what he called the Ars, a system for exploring religious and philosophical questions by combining a fixed set of basic concepts. Llull assigned letters to attributes such as goodness, greatness, and power, inscribed them on concentric paper wheels, and rotated the wheels so that every possible pairing appeared in turn. Llull himself intended the device as a tool of persuasion: he hoped that by producing every combination of divine attributes, it would lead Muslim and Jewish scholars to accept Christian doctrine through reasoning both sides already shared. Historians of computing, however, have increasingly pointed to the Ars for a different reason. Whatever its missionary purpose, the wheels carried out reasoning through a mechanical procedure, producing results by following fixed rules rather than relying on the insight of whoever turned them. It is this feature, and not Llull's theological conclusions, that later thinkers such as Gottfried Leibniz found worth developing when they imagined a calculus of thought.
input.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Llull's Ars was designed mainly to persuade Muslim and Jewish scholars, and that goal explains why historians of computing now study it closely.
Llull's Ars used lettered concentric wheels to produce pairings of divine attributes, a technique that Leibniz later adopted in order to strengthen theological arguments.
Llull's Ars, though built to serve religious persuasion, is valued today because it treated reasoning as a rule-governed procedure that later thinkers expanded on.
Llull's Ars, though built to serve religious persuasion, failed in that aim because its combinations depended on the skill of the person turning the wheels.
input.explanation: 지문은 Llull이 Ars를 종교적 설득 도구로 의도했지만 오늘날 역사가들은 그것이 고정 규칙에 따른 기계적 절차로 추론을 수행한 점 때문에 주목하며, 이 특징을 Leibniz 등이 발전시켰다고 말한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 설득 목적이 언급되긴 하지만, 지문은 역사가들이 '다른 이유로' 주목한다고 하므로 인과를 뒤집는다. B는 바퀴 구조를 정확히 묘사하지만 Leibniz가 신학적 결론이 아닌 기계적 특징을 발전시켰다는 내용과 모순된다. D는 C와 앞부분이 같으나, 지문은 결과가 돌리는 사람의 통찰에 의존하지 않는다고 했고 설득 실패도 언급하지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The text explains that Llull meant the Ars as a tool of religious persuasion, but historians now value it because it carried out reasoning through fixed rules, a feature Leibniz and others developed further. That makes C correct. A mentions the real persuasive goal, but the text says historians study the device for a different reason, so A gets the cause wrong. B describes the wheels accurately, but the text says Leibniz built on the mechanical feature, not the theological conclusions. D starts the same way as C, but the text says the results did not depend on the operator's insight, and it never says the persuasion failed.
input.design: 세부 정보(바퀴, 설득 목적, Leibniz)를 맞게 담은 오답 A·B와 정답과 같은 틀로 시작하는 D를 두어, 'however' 이후의 전환과 마지막 문장을 연결해야 정답을 고를 수 있게 했다.
